text:
I arrive at the poet's house.

A Sunday. Precisely at noon.

The room is large and quiet.

Outside, in the frozen landscape,


a raspberry-colored sun hangs

over cords of blue-gray smoke.

The scrutinizing gaze of my host

silently envelops me.


His eyes are so serene

that one could lose oneself in them forever.

I know I must be careful

not to return his gaze.


But the conversation is what I remember

from that Sunday at noon,

in the poet's broad gray house

near the gates of the Neva¹.




1914


1. Neva: Russian river that crosses the city of Saint Petersburg

translation.title: I Arrive at the Poet's House...
translation.editorial_note: This variant keeps the noon visit, Neva footnote, and dangerously serene gaze.
